newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken says it not in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken says it not in merger talks.

text.p: No merger talks are going on between Swedish banks S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, Nordbanken's chairman Jacob Palmstierna said on Tuesday.
"There are no talks whatsoever going on between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken," Palmstierna told Reuters.
When asked if this also holds true regarding Dutch bank ABN Amro he said: "Yes...that will be the same answer."
State-controlled Nordbanken and S-E-Banken announced early in February that merger talks ended without conclusion.
But analysts expect talks to resume with pressure mounting on the two banks amid a restructuring of Sweden's banking and finance sector.
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken plan to merge and Handelsbanken has bought mortgage lender Stadshypotek.
Goran Collert, the chairman of Swedbank, said in a Saturday newspaper that he expected the two big banks to merge.
Palmstierna did not want to comment on S-E-Banken's Tuesday announcement that its chief executive Bjorn Svedberg is leaving the bank.
"I can only state that it's an established custom in the business community that chief executives resign at the age of 60 and that is Svedberg's age," Palmstierna said.
